title: The kingdom splits (1 Kings 12)
hook: Rehoboam ignores the elders' counsel, and ten tribes leave

segments.voice: Yesterday, Solomon's slow turning. Your line was one small choice at a time. Did you turn one thing back a step? A new week begins, and Solomon's son faces his first test. Day seven hundred sixty-four.

A new king, a crowd, and a request. Solomon has died. His son Rehoboam goes to Shechem, where all Israel has come to make him king. Their spokesmen don't waste words: your father made our yoke heavy. Lighten the hard service and the heavy yoke, and we will serve you. Rehoboam says, go away for three days, then come back. In those three days, he asks two groups for advice. Today's word is what happens after he chooses.
screen: `A CROWD AT SHECHEM.` → `LIGHTEN OUR YOKE.` → `COME BACK IN THREE DAYS.`

segments.voice: First Kings twelve. First Rehoboam goes to the old men, in Hebrew the zekenim, the elders who had stood before his father Solomon. Their advice is simple, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever." Serve them today, and they will serve you always. Then he goes to the young men who grew up with him. Their advice is the opposite. Tell them, they say, my little finger is thicker than my father's loins. My father chastised you with whips; I will chastise you with scorpions. Rehoboam goes with the young men. On the third day he gives the people the hard answer. And the people answer back with a cry: "to your tents, O Israel; now see to thine own house, David." The northern tribes walk away and make another man their king, and only Judah stays with the house of David. A prophet had already spoken of ten tribes torn away; now it happens. Look at what the elders actually said. Not be weak. Not give in on everything. Be a servant this day. One day of humility, for a lifetime of loyalty. They had stood before Solomon; they knew his reign from the inside. The young men had grown up at the new king's side. In this story the old counsel doesn't win because it's old. It carries weight because it came from people who had seen a reign from start to finish. Rehoboam had that advice in his hands, and he chose the voices that sounded like his own.
screen: `THE ELDERS: BE A SERVANT THIS DAY.` · `THE YOUNG MEN: WHIPS AND SCORPIONS.` · `TO YOUR TENTS, O ISRAEL.` · `COUNSEL FROM THE LONG RUN.` · then, large: `THEY WILL BE THY SERVANTS FOR EVER.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: listen to an elder today. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind someone older than you, or someone who has been at something longer than you have: a grandparent, a mentor, a neighbor, a colleague with decades behind them. What advice have they given you that you brushed aside? Or what question could you ask them that you haven't yet? Let their face come to mind clearly. If you pray, you can ask to know good counsel when it comes. Then plan one call or one conversation. The bell holds the time.
Zekenim. The Hebrew word for elders, the ones Rehoboam heard out and then set aside. Today's word.
Your line: heed the old counsel. Today, ask someone who has seen the long run what they would do, and really weigh their answer. Day seven hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: Jews read the division of the kingdom in the book of Kings; from here the story follows two kingdoms, Israel in the north and Judah, where David's house reigns.

fork.setup: you're the new king. the people ask you to lighten their load. the elders say serve them today; your friends say be harder than your father. what do you do?
fork.reveal: Rehoboam followed the young men and answered roughly, and the people cried to your tents, O Israel, and the northern tribes left.

original.note: Hebrew: elders, old men. Rehoboam set aside the counsel of the zekenim.

trapdoor: what you thought: a rebellion against a weak king.
what it means: Rehoboam rejected the elders' counsel to serve, and the people left.
what a scholar hears: the elders' words turn serve around: serve them this day, and they will be thy servants for ever.

notes: 'Ten tribes' comes from Ahijah's prophecy (11:31); 12:20 says only Judah followed the house of David. The teach says 'the northern tribes' and attributes 'ten' to the prophet; the index hook says ten tribes.
'A colleague with decades behind them' in the practice is an example, not a claim.
The young men's words (12:10–11) are paraphrased.
Editor: cut the inference that the elders 'had seen what a heavy yoke cost' and changed a prayer line that echoed day 747's 'ears that can hear'.
Auditor (2026-10-01): the Judaism path quoted the KJV at 12:7 and 12:16; both now JPS 1917 (checked). Softened the narrator's verdict that the elders were simply "right".
